# Free Scrap Metal Removal: How It Works and Who Does It 

Free scrap removal is possible if you use municipal bulky‑item pickups, local scrap metal collectors, or community‑sharing platforms; paid junk‑removal companies charge only when those free routes can’t take your items. Below is a complete, step‑by‑step guide to getting your metal out of the house without spending a dime, plus an honest look at the cost of professional services when you need them.

---

## 1. What “Free Scrap Removal” Actually Means 

### Municipal bulky‑item or curbside pickup 
Most cities and counties schedule **free** bulky‑item pickups for items like appliances, metal furniture, and construction debris. 
* **How it works:** The local public works or sanitation department publishes a calendar (often monthly) for curbside collection. You place the items at the curb on the scheduled day, and the city’s own trucks haul them away at no charge. 
* **What’s accepted:** Large metal appliances (refrigerators, stoves), metal frames, old fencing, copper pipe, and sometimes mattresses (subject to a state recycling fee). 
* **Limits:** Some jurisdictions cap the volume per household (e.g., one half‑truck per pickup) and may require a permit for oversized loads. 

### Scrap metal recyclers that pay you 
Scrap yards and metal brokers will **pick up** ferrous (iron, steel) and non‑ferrous (copper, aluminum, brass) metal **for free** and pay you the market rate per pound. 
* **How it works:** Call a local recycler, give them an estimate of weight, and arrange a free haul‑away. They usually arrive with a truck, load the material, and issue a cash or check payment on the spot. 
* **What’s accepted:** Steel beams, car parts, copper wiring, aluminum siding, old gutters, and even large metal furniture. 
* **Limits:** Most recyclers require the material to be **clean** (no attached wood, plastic, or hazardous waste) and may refuse items that are too mixed or contain hazardous substances. 

### Community sharing platforms (Buy Nothing, Freecycle, Nextdoor) 
Neighbourhood groups let you **give away** scrap metal for free to anyone willing to haul it away. 
* **How it works:** Post a photo and description, specify the weight/size, and arrange a meet‑up. The taker brings a truck or trailer and loads the metal themselves. 
* **What’s accepted:** Anything you can legally give away—metal furniture, garden tools, bike frames, etc. 
* **Limits:** You are responsible for loading; the platform does not guarantee a taker, so you may need to repost or broaden the audience. 

### Retailer haul‑away programs 
Home‑improvement stores (Home Depot, Lowe’s) often run **free** haul‑away for large metal items purchased at their locations. Some will also take **unpaid** drop‑offs of metal scrap if you arrange it in advance. 
* **How it works:** Bring the item to the store’s loading dock; a staff member signs a receipt and the store loads it onto their truck. 
* **What’s accepted:** Usually only items bought at the store, but many locations will accept any clean metal for recycling. 

> **Bottom line:** Free removal exists in three main flavors—government pickups, paid‑by‑weight recyclers, and community sharing. Use them first; only turn to a paid junk‑removal service if nothing else will take your load.

---

## 2. Paid Services – When Free Options Run Out 

When you have a **mixed load**, hazardous items, or simply need the convenience of a crew that loads from inside the house, a professional junk‑removal company becomes the fallback. Below is an honest snapshot of the most common national players.

### 2.1 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? – How the pricing really works 

| Load size (truck space) | Typical price range* |
|------------------------|----------------------|
| Minimum (1/8 truck) | **$100 – $150** |
| Small loads | **$107 – $396** |
| Medium loads | **$396 – $600** |
| Large loads | **$600 – $1,099** |
| Half‑truckload | **$400 – $600** |
| Full‑truckload | **$600 – $1,000** |
| Average job (all customers) | **≈ $240** |
| Single‑item removals | **$70 – $400** (depends on bulk & weight) |
| Mattress (recycling fee) | **$70 – $100** + **$10.50** (CA, CT, RI) |
| Sofa / couch | **$59 – $170** (varies by zip) |

\*Ranges reflect all U.S. markets; high‑cost metros (NYC, SF, Seattle) sit at the upper end, while mid‑west and southern metros sit near the lower end.

**What the price includes** 
All labor, loading from anywhere on the property (no curb‑only rule), hauling, disposal and recycling fees, and post‑job cleanup. Crews are licensed and insured.

**How booking works** 
* Book online or call 1‑800‑468‑5865. 
* No price quote is given online or over the phone. 
* A free on‑site estimate is provided; no credit card is required. 
* The crew calls 25‑30 minutes before arrival; same‑day service is often possible. 

**Flex product** – If you can load a bag or container yourself, Flex starts at **$39** for collection only.

### 2.2 Competitor snapshot (price‑only data) 

| Company | Minimum charge | Volume‑based range (half‑truck) | Notable notes |
|---------|----------------|--------------------------------|---------------|
| **LoadUp** | **$89** minimum | N/A (price per item) – guaranteed online | Prices lock in at booking; 20‑30 % lower than most rivals |
| **Junk King** | **$99** minimum | **$389 – $488** (half‑truck) | Approximate online estimate; some states not covered |
| **College Hunks Hauling Junk** | **$150** (low end) | **$150 – $750** (full job) | $99 dispatch fee often appears after booking |

All three companies include labor, loading, haul‑away, and disposal, but the **exact volume** they consider “half‑truck” can differ because truck dimensions vary by franchise.

### 2.3 How to squeeze the most value from a paid service 

* **Consolidate** every item you can into one truck; two half‑loads cost more than one full load. 
* **Share** a truck with a neighbor—most crews will split the price proportionally. 
* **Schedule mid‑week** or off‑season pickups; crews have more flexibility and may offer a lower on‑site estimate. 
* **Pre‑sort** metal from non‑metal junk; a cleaner load loads faster, reducing labor time. 
* **Get 2‑3 quotes** and compare the on‑site estimate (not the advertised minimum). 

> **Important discount truth:** There is **no official military, senior, student, or AAA discount** for 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK?. Coupon sites often list codes,” but they are **unverified and usually expired**. The only reliable way to save is by joining the company’s email list (you’ll receive $10‑$25 off codes) or hunting for local franchise promotions.

*If you’ve exhausted free options and need a guaranteed pick‑up, consider getting a free on‑site estimate from a reputable junk‑removal service. Compare the estimate with the free routes above to ensure you’re not overpaying.*

## 3. Step‑by‑Step Guide to Getting Free Scrap Metal Out of Your Home 

### 3.1 Identify what you have 
* List every metal item (refrigerator, steel fence, copper pipe, aluminum siding). 
* Estimate weight (a standard refrigerator ≈ 150 lb, a 10‑ft steel fence ≈ 300 lb). 

### 3.2 Clean and separate 
* Remove non‑metal parts (plastic, wood, insulation). 
* Rinse off oil or chemicals—many recyclers won’t take contaminated metal. 

### 3.3 Choose the right free channel 

| Item type | Best free route | Why |
|-----------|----------------|-----|
| Large appliances (fridge, dryer) | Municipal bulky‑item pickup | City trucks accept whole appliances, no need to load yourself |
| Clean ferrous metal (steel, iron) | Local scrap recycler (pay‑you) | You earn cash; recycler provides free haul‑away |
| Non‑ferrous metal (copper, brass) | Scrap recycler (pay‑you) | Higher per‑pound rates; many recyclers specialize in non‑ferrous |
| Mixed metal furniture | Buy Nothing / Freecycle | Community members often have a truck and will take it for free |
| Small metal parts (bicycle frames, toolboxes) | Retailer haul‑away or community group | Easy to drop off at a local store or hand‑off to a neighbour |

### 3.4 Contact and schedule 
* **Municipal pickup:** Call your city’s sanitation department or check the website for the next curbside date. 
* **Scrap recycler:** Search “scrap metal recycler near me,” call for a free quote, confirm they’ll pick up. 
* **Community group:** Post a clear photo, describe weight, and propose a pick‑up window. 

### 3.5 Load and drop‑off (if required) 
* For municipal pickups, simply place items at the curb before the scheduled time. 
* For recyclers, have a clear path to the driveway; the crew will load directly from your property. 
* For community groups, meet at a neutral location (e.g., a park) if you can’t bring the items to the taker. 

### 3.6 Verify paperwork 
* **Recyclers:** Ask for a receipt that states the weight and price paid. 
* **Municipal pickup:** Keep the city’s pickup schedule as proof in case of disputes.

## 4. Worked Dollar Example – How a Small Load Costs with 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? 

Imagine you have a **half‑truckload** of mixed scrap metal and a broken sofa. The crew estimates the load occupies **5 ft × 5 ft × 8 ft** (half‑truck dimensions). 

1. **Base price range for half‑truck:** **$400 – $600**. 
2. **Add‑on for a sofa:** The sofa falls in the **$59 – $170** range (depends on zip). 
3. **Total estimated cost:** 

```
Low end = $400 (half‑truck) + $59 (sofa) = $459
High end = $600 (half‑truck) + $170 (sofa) = $770
```

4. **Average job comparison:** The national **average job** is **≈ $240**. Because your load is larger than average, you’ll pay roughly **$460‑$770**, which is **2‑3 ×** the average. 

If you could instead split the metal with a neighbour, each would pay roughly half of the half‑truck price (**$200‑$300**) and avoid the sofa surcharge, saving **$260‑$470**.

## 5. Common Mistakes People Make 

| Mistake | Why it hurts you | How to avoid it |
|---------|------------------|-----------------|
| **Assuming “free” means no effort** | Many free routes require you to load the items yourself, which can be unsafe or time‑consuming. | Plan a loading strategy (use a dolly, enlist a friend) before the pickup date. |
| **Mixing hazardous waste with metal** | Scrap yards will refuse contaminated loads, forcing you to pay a removal service later. | Separate batteries, chemicals, and asbestos‑containing parts before contacting a recycler. |
| **Skipping the on‑site estimate** | Some people quote a price over the phone and get surprised by a higher on‑site estimate. | Always request the free on‑site estimate; no credit card is needed. |
| **Over‑loading the municipal curb** | Exceeding the city’s volume limit can result in a fine or the truck refusing your load. | Check your city’s volume cap; if you have more, schedule a second curbside date or use a recycler for the excess. |
| **Relying on expired coupon codes** | Entering a dead code wastes time and may lead you to think the service is more expensive than it is. | Join the company’s email list for verified discounts, or look for local franchise promotions. |
| **Not pre‑sorting** | Crews spend extra labor loading mixed items, which can push the estimate higher. | Separate metal from wood, plastic, and electronics before the crew arrives. |

---

## 6. Frequently Asked Questions 

**Q1. How do I know if my city offers free bulky‑item pickup?** 
Check the official website of your city’s public works or sanitation department. Look for “bulk waste,” “large item pickup,” or “metal collection” calendars. If the info isn’t obvious, call the department’s customer service line.

**Q2. Will a scrap metal recycler pay me for a broken refrigerator?** 
Yes, if the refrigerator is **clean** (no foam insulation, oil, or refrigerant leaks). Most recyclers will pay a per‑pound rate for steel and a higher rate for copper components like the compressor.

**Q3. Is it legal to leave metal junk on the curb without a scheduled pickup?** 
No. Most municipalities consider unattended items “illegal dumping.” Always schedule a pickup or place the items in a designated bulk‑waste container.

**Q4. Do I need a permit to have a recycler haul away a full truckload?** 
Usually not for residential properties, but some cities require a **permit** for oversized loads that exceed curb width or block traffic. Verify with your local authority if the truck will need to park on the street.

**Q5. How much does a mattress recycling fee add to the cost?** 
In California, Connecticut, and Rhode Island the state‑mandated fee is **$10.50 per mattress** under the 2026 Bye Bye Mattress program. 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? may pass this fee through to you.

**Q6. Can I combine a free community pickup with a paid service in one trip?** 
Yes. You can arrange for a neighbour to take the metal items for free, then have a paid service handle the remaining non‑metal junk. This reduces the paid crew’s volume and can lower the final estimate.

---

## 7. Bottom‑Line Takeaway 

*Start with the truly free routes—municipal bulk pickups, paid‑by‑weight scrap recyclers, and community sharing groups. Only turn to a paid junk‑removal company like 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? when those options can’t handle the volume, weight, or convenience you need. By consolidating loads, scheduling wisely, and pre‑sorting, you can often avoid any cost or even earn cash for your scrap metal.*
